gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many nights each wireless pick lasts on one charge when it is connected the way an Xbox owner uses it (through the 2.4 GHz dongle) and measured by a reviewer: at 3 h a night the Stealth 600 Gen 3 lasts about 28 nights, the Arctis Nova 5X about 14 and the Xbox Wireless Headset at most about 7.
standout_why: Neither cited rival (RTINGS best-for-Xbox and Tom's Guide best gaming headsets) gave readable figures through the fetcher: both returned only navigation text, so I could not confirm whether they derive anything. TechRadar's excerpt had no battery figures. Adellion (rank 10, not cited) does compute nights between charges at 3 h a night, but it uses claimed figures that are wrong for Xbox use: 60 h for the Nova 5X, which is SteelSeries' Bluetooth rating, giving about 20 nights; and 15 h for the Xbox Wireless Headset, which is the original model's rating, giving about 5 nights. No page I read uses the Nova 5X's 2.4 GHz rating (50 h) or a reviewer-measured runtime (42 h 10 min). That cuts its nights from 20 to 14. No page gives charge minutes per 3-hour session either.
decides: This backs the Stealth 600 Gen 3 as the battery-life pick: it lasts twice as many nights as the Nova 5X and costs $40 less. It costs $1.31 per tested hour against $3.56 for the Nova 5X. It also undercuts ChatGPT's 'up to 60-hour battery' line for the Nova 5X, its 'best overall value' pick, because 60 h is the Bluetooth figure, not the Xbox one. The Xbox Wireless Headset's case rests on connecting with no dongle, not on battery: it needs a charge about weekly and 22.5 min of fast charging to cover one 3-hour session.

findings.note: Reviewer's observation. The review gives no quick-charge figure.

findings.label: Measured runtime on the 2.4 GHz dongle
findings.note: Measured on a PC through the USB-C 2.4 GHz dongle at about 50% volume. SteelSeries rates it 50 h on 2.4 GHz and 60 h on Bluetooth. Xbox game audio uses the 2.4 GHz dongle, not Bluetooth.

findings.label: Nights per charge at 3 h/night (measured, dongle)
findings.note: 42.17 h ÷ 3 = 14.1. On the 2.4 GHz rating: 50 ÷ 3 = 16.7. Adellion's 20 nights comes from the 60 h Bluetooth rating.

findings.source_title: GameStop: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X Wireless Headset
findings.note: The listing says '6 hours of use in just 15 minutes', and SoundGuys gives the same figure. 15 min × 3 h ÷ 6 h = 7.5 min, assuming the charge rate is linear.
